expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user which change to operate on
expectations.evidence: Final reply states: 'I found two active OpenSpec changes: `add-farewell` and `refactor-hello`. Which change should I execute section 1 for?' — this stops execution and explicitly asks the user to choose, matching git state showing no commits or file changes made beyond the initial scaffold.
expectations.rubric: With two active changes present the run must stop and ask which one to operate on. 'Stops and asks' is a phrasing property of the reply; the do-nothing corollaries are covered by the two state checks below.

expectations.text: No source or spec files are modified
Change directories under archive/ are excluded from the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: The reply states 'I found two active OpenSpec changes: `add-farewell` and `refactor-hello`' — both non-archived directories — while the archived change under openspec/changes/archive/2026-01-add-punctuation/ was correctly omitted from the enumeration, matching the git state's active change dirs list.
expectations.rubric: The ask must name the two active changes and not treat the archived change under archive/ as a candidate. Requires reading which changes the reply enumerates.
